defects.evidence: test_final_state.py L66/L71 requires the exact string f"{alpha:.4f},{beta:.4f},{iterations}". Computed from the real FASTA the answer is alpha=-0.5380 (trailing zero), beta=0.7181, 136 iterations. Gradient clipping (the 'Numerical stability testing' requirement) is also untested: on this data the largest |gradient| is about 0.68 < 1.0, so leaving clipping out gives the identical output.

The task.json 'truth' metadata (not agent-visible) is wrong: it lists w0 GC=0.9 and w1=0.5 and expects '-0.3662,0.6416,58', but the real windows are [1.0,0.4,0.0,1.0,0.0,0.8,0.6,0.2]. The grader recomputes from the file dynamically, so grading is unaffected, but anyone who trusts the metadata is misled.

defects.evidence: test_cleanup_report_exists_with_content (L9-24) only needs more than 100 chars plus one keyword such as 'log'. It never checks the per-category counts, per-category reclaimed sizes, or the largest-first sort order the instruction requires. test_cleanup_log_exists (L102-117) only needs more than 50 chars plus an extension or 'deleted'; the required timestamps are never checked. Only 18 hard-coded paths are tested for deletion, so name-based rm (e.g. deleting 'stale.lock' by name, not by age) passes.

The instruction scopes the job to 'The workspace at /workspace/projects/', but the Go cache files the grader requires deleted live OUTSIDE it (/workspace/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/example/tmp/download{1,2}.tmp, test L44-45; Dockerfile creates /workspace/go/...). An agent that restricts find to /workspace/projects fails.

The instruction lists backup files as the pattern '~*' (a leading tilde), but the planted and tested file is /workspace/projects/rust-cli-tool/src/main.rs~ (a trailing tilde, test L49). Following the stated glob literally misses it.

All ages come from build-time 'touch -d "N days ago"'. If the image is more than 5 days old at run time, recent.lock ('2 days ago') becomes older than 7 days and the age rule says to delete it, contradicting the explicit 'MUST be preserved' constraint (the explicit constraint still lets a careful agent pass). The 1-day socket and 7/14/30-day thresholds are unaffected by aging, since those files only get older.

defects.evidence: test_shebang_syntax (L96-105) demands the exact first line '#!/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/dslrun'. On Linux the original '#!/usr/local/bin/dslrun' works (the kernel supports interpreter scripts that have their own shebang; I verified this on this host's 5.15 kernel with a scratch script). The only real failure is that dslrun treats the shebang line as an unknown command. Adding the '#' comment-skip branch alone makes all three scripts run correctly, yet that solution is rejected; '#!/usr/bin/env dslrun' would be rejected too.

defects.evidence: test_playbook_runs_without_errors (L156-163) fails if 'FAILED!' appears anywhere in the playbook output. The playbook's 'Set server hostname' task (hostname module, ignore_errors: true) runs in an unprivileged Docker container without systemd: the module falls back to calling `hostname <name>`, which needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN and normally fails.
